Point chi-square: numerical accuracy and CPU compatibility

Technical report · 21 September 2026

The existing CPU recurrence and JAX direct-phase implementation evaluate the same chi-square statistic through different floating-point operations. On the captured search inputs, these choices produce a small but reproducible difference that exceeds the project's CPU-compatibility tolerance. Direct Fourier sums agree more closely with an independent double-precision inverse FFT on the examples checked. Compatibility with existing CPU outputs remains a separate, unchanged requirement for the JAX acceleration work.

This report describes an engineering tradeoff between established numerical behavior and an alternative evaluation of the same formula. Both output compatibility and numerical agreement are useful objectives. The recurrence is an economical way to evaluate selected time samples without performing a separate transform for every frequency bin. Its finite-precision behavior becomes relevant here because the bins are long and the output-comparison tolerance is tight.

Scope and provenance

The evidence comes from the 20 September qualification run of pycbc_inspiral on len: 32 distinct compressed IMRPhenomD templates, H1 strain, 2,048 Hz sampling, complex64 correlation arrays, 512-second segments, 16 chi-square bins and a 30 Hz low-frequency cutoff. The FFT length is 1,048,576 samples. Search GPS bounds were 1187007048–1187009080; configured trigger bounds were 1187007160–1187009064. The SNR threshold was 5.5 and the NewSNR threshold 5. These are qualification observations, not timing samples.

The original CPU checkout was clean at revision 40e94792b3edf59f39b18b65102b28a4f74433a7. The candidate was a frozen dirty checkout based on 379a0579b725c52177bfeb244f5fecc2289bd226; its tracked patch SHA-256 was 9410032fb026ae1893a1309976d9a4ad7ef169b6431086ffff355976d607b91a. The campaign also records untracked-file hashes. A commit identifier alone does not specify that candidate. Code links below refer to retained, line-numbered snapshots of the measured source, not a moving branch.

The measurement environment used Python 3.11, NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.13.0, JAX 0.4.20 and jaxlib 0.4.20+cuda12.cudnn89, with an RTX 4090 for the CUDA arm. The ordinary candidate CPU and original CPU produced identical retained chi-square values. The JAX CPU and CUDA arms matched all 77 retained trigger identities, but each exceeded the chi-square tolerance on 72 values. The campaign stopped before timing, live qualification or profiling.

An observer replayed the original CPU command and returned its original results unchanged, while evaluating alternative sums on copies of the same correlations. All 77 retained CPU chi-square outputs replayed exactly. The observer recorded 67 point-evaluation calls containing 89 points before the NewSNR cut, and saved the first six correlation arrays, containing 11 points, for independent checks. The six captures were selected by call order, not by discrepancy. The illustrative example below is explicitly selected from them for its large difference.

This is a numerical-accuracy limitation of the existing CPU point routine under the tested conditions. It can arise in ordinary, unmodified searches: SingleDetPowerChisq.values, lines 385–390 calls that routine. Phase drift here means accumulated rounding as the routine traverses frequency samples within a bin, with a reset at each bin boundary. It does not mean drift accumulating over hours of detector time. Other chi-square paths use full FFTs and do not use this particular recurrence. The observed output discrepancy is established; its consequences for search sensitivity or false-alarm rates have not been measured.

The common mathematical calculation

Let c k be the precomputed correlation spectrum, n a selected time-sample index, N the full transform length, and B b = [ l b , u b ) one of p frequency bins. Its unnormalized partial matched-filter amplitude is

z b ( n ) = ∑ k = l b u b − 1 c k exp ⁡ ( 2 π i k n / N ) .

Given the precomputed unnormalized full SNR z ( n ) and normalization A , PyCBC evaluates

χ 2 ( n ) = A 2 [ p ∑ b = 1 p | z b ( n ) | 2 − | z ( n ) | 2 ] .

This is the expression in original chisq.py, lines 136–138. It is the unreduced chi-square statistic, not chi-square divided by its degrees of freedom. Every controlled comparison holds the correlation, bin edges, selected indices, saved SNR and normalization fixed. The diagnostic therefore addresses evaluation of the bin sums, rather than a change to the statistic, data conditioning or template physics.

How the implementations evaluate it

Existing CPU point routine. For each bin and selected sample, the routine initializes a phase q l b and a rotation r , then advances through the bin:

q l b = e 2 π i l b n / N , r = e 2 π i n / N , q k + 1 = q k r .

The initialization uses C sin and cos with the literal 3.141592653 for pi. For complex64 correlations, the stored phases, rotation, arithmetic temporaries and accumulators are float32. The phase is reinitialized at each bin boundary. See precision selection, lines 9–15 and 140–155 and initialization, lines 83–89.

The routine also uses a three-product form of complex multiplication. Writing c k = v r + i v i and q k = t 1 + i t 2 , it computes

a = v r ( t 1 + t 2 ) , b = t 1 ( v i − v r ) , d = t 2 ( v r + v i ) , c k q k = ( a − d ) + i ( a + b ) .

That identity is exact in real arithmetic. Its rounding need not match the usual four-product complex multiplication. A compatibility implementation must consider both the recurrence and these accumulation operations, shown in chisq_cpu.pyx, lines 91–121.

Current JAX direct-phase path. Each phase is formed independently using

m = ( k n ) mod N , q k = exp ⁡ ( 2 π i m / N ) .

The product and remainder use int64 and are exact for the captured sizes; the angle and exponential are evaluated at double precision, then the CUDA phase is cast to the correlation dtype. This keeps the angle within one rotation and avoids carrying a previous phase's rounding into the next. See chisq_jax.py, lines 85–93.

The CPU and CUDA paths then differ:

  • Under the JAX CPU scheme, a NumPy helper sums products in complex128, accumulates powers in float64, and returns float32 powers for complex64 inputs. See chisq_numpy.py, lines 20–46 and CPU dispatch, lines 182–190.

  • On CUDA, complex64 products enter a cumulative sum. Bin amplitudes are differences between cumulative sums at the bin boundaries. This still has rounding and possible cancellation; it is not an exact or entirely double-precision calculation. See scalar core, lines 102–113 and batched core, lines 144–165.

The benchmark correlation arrays are complex64 throughout. Higher-precision temporary phase calculations do not change that input-array policy.

Measured compatibility and numerical agreement

The existing acceptance rule is

| x − x ref | ≤ 10 − 5 + 10 − 4 | x ref | .

For compatibility, x ref is always the original CPU output. Changing only the point-sum calculation, on the original CPU inputs, reproduces the observed disagreement:

Independent FFT controls

For each of the six captured correlations, the diagnostic puts one bin into a zero-padded complex128 array and evaluates N * scipy.fft.ifft(band) at the saved sample indices. Multiplication by N reverses SciPy's inverse FFT normalization. It then applies the same chi-square expression, holding the saved complex64 SNR term and normalization fixed. This uses a different evaluation algorithm from the direct-phase helper.

These experiments do not separately measure the contribution of every multiplication, phase update and accumulation. The complex128 runs are diagnostic controls only, not additional benchmarks.

Why a small phase rounding can accumulate

In exact arithmetic | r | = 1 . A stored float32 rotation generally has a slightly different modulus and angle. Repeated multiplication propagates both that representation error and rounding from each update. For example, if | r ~ | = 1 + ϵ , even exact repetition of that rounded rotation would multiply the modulus by ( 1 + ϵ ) j after j steps. The phase error also accumulates. Resetting the phase at a bin boundary limits this sequence to the bin width; the widest observed bin had 396,226 frequency samples.

For this example, the rounded rotation has modulus 1.000000027152669. After 373,307 updates, the explicit model's phase modulus is approximately 1.0100972, and its wrapped phase difference is approximately -0.00249489 radians. The directly formed complex64 endpoint phase has a modulus difference of approximately 2.72e-8 and phase difference 6.37e-9 radians. The initial recurrence phase also includes the CPU pi constant's argument difference. The figure illustrates a mechanism; its phase error is not a prediction of the full chi-square error.

The final chi-square also subtracts two quantities. Relative error can be sensitive to cancellation when their difference is small. No separate cancellation error budget was measured here. Likewise, CUDA prefix-sum subtraction has its own precision tradeoffs. Independent phases remove the long phase-update chain, not all floating-point error.

Complex128: precision helps, while the pi constant remains

The original CPU routine supports complex128 inputs. Its dtype selection, lines 141–154 then selects float64 phases, rotations, multiplication temporaries, accumulators and output through the fused types declared at lines 9–15. The recurrence and three-product multiplication stay the same. Higher precision reduces rounding at each step; it does not eliminate rounding or change the phase initialization constant.

Controlled change of arithmetic precision. The observer passed corr.astype(numpy.complex128) to the original compiled CPU shift_sum. The saved complex64 correlation values are exactly representable after this conversion; it adds no information to them. Bin edges, sample indices, the saved complex64 SNR-power term and normalization were held fixed. These controls therefore isolate the point routine's arithmetic, rather than re-running conditioning, waveform generation or a complete search in double precision. The source and observed outputs are retained in the evidence bundle.

For the 11 captured points in Figure 2, the maximum relative CPU/FFT difference falls from 1.73394e-3 (0.173394%) with complex64 to 1.41124e-5 (0.00141124%) with complex128. The first maximum is about 123 times the second. These are maxima over the same population, potentially at different points, not a uniform per-point improvement factor or an isolated error budget. Nine complex64 values exceed the tolerance when compared with the FFT; none of the 11 complex128 controls do. This is a numerical comparison to the FFT, not CPU-compatibility qualification.

Why a residual remains. The literal 3.141592653 is unchanged in the double-precision specialization. Using more precise arithmetic cannot recover the missing digits of that literal. If its value is denoted π c , its contribution to the unwrapped phase difference at frequency index k is, in exact arithmetic,

Δ θ k = 2 ( π c − π ) k n / N .

This includes the initial phase at the bin boundary as well as subsequent rotations. Large k n / N can make the phase difference relevant even though π c − π is small. Direct complex128 sums using the same literal agree with the compiled complex128 recurrence to within 2.12e-11 relative on these 11 chi-square values. Their maximum difference from the FFT is also 1.41124e-5. The paired controls support the pi constant and associated initialization arithmetic as accounting for the observed double-precision residual at this scale.

For an additional control, the report generator forms each phase independently using integer modular cycles and full double-precision numpy.pi, sums in complex128, and retains float64 bin powers and the final chi-square. It holds the same saved SNR term and normalization fixed. These direct sums agree with the independent FFT to approximately 8e-16 relative in the local regeneration. This control is not a measurement of a modified Cython kernel or a complex128 JAX CUDA search.

At the final plotted frequency, the float64 model with the original pi constant has a modulus error of approximately 5.76e-12 and a phase difference of -3.86966e-4 radians. The model using full double-precision pi has modulus error 1.36e-11 and phase difference -2.52e-10 radians. Thus increasing precision sharply reduces modulus drift, while the pi constant still produces an angle bias. Changing that constant alone is not guaranteed to improve every component of every result; here the full-pi model has a slightly larger, but still tiny, modulus error. Compiler contraction and trigonometric-library differences may alter a compiled recurrence's exact trace.

Compatibility and scope. On the 77 retained points, the compiled complex128 control is within 2.06086e-5 relative of the float32-output direct sums. However, it differs from the original complex64 CPU outputs by up to 1.88980e-3 relative, exceeding the original-CPU tolerance on 72 of 77 values. Promoting the calculation to complex128 therefore does not satisfy the established compatibility requirement. The compatible mode therefore retains the requested original precision and recurrence.

This analysis establishes a numerical limitation and its precision dependence for the captured inputs. It does not determine the effect on detection sensitivity or false-alarm rates. No production CPU code or pi constant was changed. The maintained performance benchmarks remain at 2,048 Hz with complex64 search arrays; these complex128 controls provide neither complete-search qualification nor performance measurements.

A compatible and explicit JAX mode selection

The JAX scheme now provides two point chi-square modes. They apply to pycbc_inspiral, pycbc_live and the scalar and batched triggered-point APIs:

--processing-scheme jax:cuda:0 --jax-chisq-mode cpu-compatible
--processing-scheme jax:cuda:0 --jax-chisq-mode direct-phase

cpu-compatible is the default. On CUDA, chisq_jax_compat.py implements the CPU recurrence in JAX: phase initialization uses the CPU pi constant, phase state and sums retain the input precision, and each frequency update consumes the preceding state. Independent points and bins run in parallel; bin powers are combined in order. Groups of 16 dependent frequency steps reduce device launch overhead. Cropped correlations retain the original absolute bin origin and phase evolution through omitted zeros. Correlations stay on the GPU; the public API returns the small power array to the host. On JAX CPU, this mode calls the existing compiled CPU point routine.

direct-phase selects the independently evaluated Fourier phases analyzed above. The API spelling is JAXScheme("cuda:0", chisq_mode="direct-phase"). Mode selection is part of the scheme cache key and is recorded in benchmark commands, scientific evidence and receipts. An explicit mode is rejected for non-JAX schemes. Ordinary CPU dispatch and the full time-series FFT chi-square path are unchanged.

Compatibility means agreement with the compiled CPU reference within the established tolerance, not bitwise portability. The CPU extension uses compiler optimizations including fast-math; JAX/XLA versions and device instruction contraction can also affect rounding. Preserving the recurrence is necessary here, but measured qualification remains necessary.

Implemented-mode qualification, 21 September. The same 32-template, 2,048 Hz, complex64 inspiral workload was rerun against the frozen original CPU outputs. Every scientific gate passed for branch CPU, JAX CPU and JAX CUDA, with zero missing gates and the same 77 retained trigger identities. The ordinary branch CPU chi-square values were exactly unchanged.

The CUDA result uses the on-device JAX recurrence, with no CPU point-routine fallback. A device-residency regression test checks that path. Separate captured-input checks passed all 11 points in both precisions: maximum relative bin-power differences were 1.47966e-5 for complex64 and 2.48939e-12 for complex128 against their respective compiled CPU references. The complex128 inputs promote the captured complex64 arrays; they are arithmetic controls, not a complex128 search qualification.

The tested CUDA environment is JAX 0.4.20 on the RTX 4090 described above. Unit coverage includes cropped and full correlations, empty bins and points, thresholded candidates, mode isolation and both precisions. Tests of cpu-compatible use the compiled CPU reference; tests of direct-phase use independent Fourier/FFT controls. Requiring both modes to match both references at the same tight tolerance on the captured complex64 inputs would conflict with the measured separation.

These results qualify this inspiral workload. Complete pycbc_live qualification and fresh full-process performance measurements remain to be run; helper timings do not establish an executable speedup. No full performance campaign was restarted for this implementation check.

Evidence, reproduction and limits

The evidence supports the narrower statement that the current direct-phase evaluation agrees more closely with an independent FFT on these captured inputs. It is not a claim of universal superiority, exact arithmetic, improved detection sensitivity, a measured change in false-alarm rates, or complete-search compatibility. The original CPU routine and comparison tolerances are unchanged. The switch is implemented and the qualification above is separate from the direct-phase observations in the main numerical analysis. Full-process speed measurements remain pending.

The repository contains tools/report_jax_chisq_numerics.py. With NumPy, SciPy, h5py, Matplotlib and docutils installed, this regenerates all four figures, machine-readable tables, source pages and an offline HTML report:

python tools/report_jax_chisq_numerics.py \
  --evidence artifacts/jax-chisq-diagnosis-20260920 \
  --output docs/_static/jax_chisq_numerics \
  --render docs/jax_chisq_numerics.rst

The evidence directory contains the six point-input-*.npz arrays, points.json, the earlier analysis.json, four saved qualification trigger files under qualification/, and measured sources under source/. It also retains the original replay scripts and native-probe-science.json. Raw evidence is an artifact, not a Git-tracked input. The local archive artifacts/jax-chisq-numerics-evidence-20260921.tar.gz preserves these files, source provenance, and the report generator. Extract it at the repository root before running the command above. SHA-256 input hashes and the generator hash are in the manifest.

The implemented-mode check has a separate local evidence archive, artifacts/jax-chisq-mode-evidence-20260921.tar.gz. It preserves the qualification commands, trigger outputs, comparison results, CUDA test log, and the exact source overlay used for that check. Its README describes run_qualification.py, verify_qualification.py and the captured-input precision check. Replaying the searches requires the frozen benchmark inputs and original CPU evidence at the paths recorded in those commands. The compatibility JSON files linked above come from these checks; the report generator does not rerun them.

The generator recomputes the independent inverse FFTs, direct complex128 controls, and float32/float64 phase illustrations. It reads the observed compiled CPU and JAX outputs; it does not pretend to rerun those kernels or the full search. It checks the regenerated comparisons against the saved diagnostic summary, verifies trigger identities, and checks exact CPU replay and branch CPU agreement. The HTML embeds figures, tables and referenced source listings for offline reading. PNG and SVG versions of the figures are also retained separately.

  33  def power_chisq_bins_from_sigmasq_series(sigmasq_series, num_bins, kmin, kmax):
  34      """Returns bins of equal power for use with the chisq functions
  35  
  36      Parameters
  37      ----------
  38  
  39      sigmasq_series: FrequencySeries
  40          A frequency series containing the cumulative power of a filter template
  41          preweighted by a psd.
  42      num_bins: int
  43          The number of chisq bins to calculate.
  44      kmin: int
  45          DOCUMENTME
  46      kmax: int
  47          DOCUMENTME
  48  
  49      Returns
  50      -------
  51  
  52      bins: List of ints
  53          A list of the edges of the chisq bins is returned.
  54      """
  55      sigmasq = sigmasq_series[kmax - 1]
  56      edge_vec = numpy.arange(0, num_bins) * sigmasq / num_bins
  57      bins = numpy.searchsorted(sigmasq_series[kmin:kmax], edge_vec, side='right')
  58      bins += kmin
  59      return numpy.append(bins, kmax)

 111  def power_chisq_at_points_from_precomputed(corr, snr, snr_norm, bins, indices):
 112      """Calculate the chisq timeseries from precomputed values for only select points.
 113  
 114      This function calculates the chisq at each point by explicitly time shifting
 115      and summing each bin. No FFT is involved.
 116  
 117      Parameters
 118      ----------
 119      corr: FrequencySeries
 120          The product of the template and data in the frequency domain.
 121      snr: numpy.ndarray
 122          The unnormalized array of snr values at only the selected points in `indices`.
 123      snr_norm: float
 124          The normalization of the snr (EXPLAINME : refer to Findchirp paper?)
 125      bins: List of integers
 126          The edges of the equal power bins
 127      indices: Array
 128          The indices where we will calculate the chisq. These must be relative
 129          to the given `corr` series.
 130  
 131      Returns
 132      -------
 133      chisq: Array
 134          An array containing only the chisq at the selected points.
 135      """
 136      num_bins = len(bins) - 1
 137      chisq = shift_sum(corr, indices, bins) # pylint:disable=assignment-from-no-return
 138      return (chisq * num_bins - (snr.conj() * snr).real) * (snr_norm ** 2.0)

 196      for j in range(num_bins):
 197          k_min = int(bins[j])
 198          k_max = int(bins[j+1])
 199  
 200          qtilde[k_min:k_max] = corr[k_min:k_max]
 201          pycbc.fft.ifft(qtilde, q)
 202          qtilde[k_min:k_max].clear()
 203  
 204          if return_bins:
 205              bin_snrs.append(TimeSeries(q  * snr_norm *  num_bins ** 0.5,
 206                                        delta_t=snr.delta_t,
 207                                        epoch=snr.start_time))
 208  
 209          if indices is not None:
 210              chisq_accum_bin(chisq, q.take(indices))
 211          else:
 212              chisq_accum_bin(chisq, q)
 213  
 214      chisq = (chisq * num_bins - snr.squared_norm()) * (snr_norm ** 2.0)
 215  
 216      if indices is None:
 217          chisq = TimeSeries(chisq, delta_t=snr.delta_t, epoch=snr.start_time, copy=False)
 218  
 219      if return_bins:
 220          return chisq, bin_snrs
 221      else:
 222          return chisq

 225  def fastest_power_chisq_at_points(corr, snr, snrv, snr_norm, bins, indices):
 226      """Calculate the chisq values for only selected points.
 227  
 228      This function looks at the number of points to be evaluated and selects
 229      the fastest method (FFT, or direct time shift and sum). In either case,
 230      only the selected points are returned.
 231  
 232      Parameters
 233      ----------
 234      corr: FrequencySeries
 235          The product of the template and data in the frequency domain.
 236      snr: Array
 237          The unnormalized snr
 238      snr_norm: float
 239          The snr normalization factor  --- EXPLAINME
 240      bins: List of integers
 241          The edges of the equal power bins
 242      indices: Array
 243          The indices where we will calculate the chisq. These must be relative
 244          to the given `snr` series.
 245  
 246      Returns
 247      -------
 248      chisq: Array
 249          An array containing only the chisq at the selected points.
 250      """
 251      import pycbc.scheme
 252      if isinstance(pycbc.scheme.mgr.state, pycbc.scheme.CPUScheme):
 253          # We don't have that many points so do the direct time shift.
 254          return power_chisq_at_points_from_precomputed(corr, snrv,
 255                                                        snr_norm, bins, indices)
 256      else:
 257          # We have a lot of points so it is faster to use the fourier transform
 258          return power_chisq_from_precomputed(corr, snr, snr_norm, bins,
 259                                              indices=indices)

 262  def power_chisq(template, data, num_bins, psd,
 263                  low_frequency_cutoff=None,
 264                  high_frequency_cutoff=None,
 265                  return_bins=False):
 266      """Calculate the chisq timeseries
 267  
 268      Parameters
 269      ----------
 270      template: FrequencySeries or TimeSeries
 271          A time or frequency series that contains the filter template.
 272      data: FrequencySeries or TimeSeries
 273          A time or frequency series that contains the data to filter. The length
 274          must be commensurate with the template.
 275          (EXPLAINME - does this mean 'the same as' or something else?)
 276      num_bins: int
 277          The number of frequency bins used for chisq. The number of statistical
 278          degrees of freedom ('dof') is 2*num_bins-2.
 279      psd: FrequencySeries
 280          The psd of the data.
 281      low_frequency_cutoff: {None, float}, optional
 282          The low frequency cutoff for the filter
 283      high_frequency_cutoff: {None, float}, optional
 284          The high frequency cutoff for the filter
 285      return_bins: {boolean, False}, optional
 286          Return a list of the individual chisq bins
 287  
 288      Returns
 289      -------
 290      chisq: TimeSeries
 291          TimeSeries containing the chisq values for all times.
 292      """
 293      htilde = make_frequency_series(template)
 294      stilde = make_frequency_series(data)
 295  
 296      bins = power_chisq_bins(htilde, num_bins, psd, low_frequency_cutoff,
 297                              high_frequency_cutoff)
 298      corra = zeros((len(htilde) - 1) * 2, dtype=htilde.dtype)
 299      total_snr, corr, tnorm = matched_filter_core(htilde, stilde, psd,
 300                             low_frequency_cutoff, high_frequency_cutoff,
 301                             corr_out=corra)
 302  
 303      return power_chisq_from_precomputed(corr, total_snr, tnorm, bins, return_bins=return_bins)

 306  class SingleDetPowerChisq(object):
 307      """Class that handles precomputation and memory management for efficiently
 308      running the power chisq in a single detector inspiral analysis.
 309      """
 310      def __init__(self, num_bins=0, snr_threshold=None):
 311          if not (num_bins == "0" or num_bins == 0):
 312              self.do = True
 313              self.column_name = "chisq"
 314              self.table_dof_name = "chisq_dof"
 315              self.num_bins = num_bins
 316          else:
 317              self.do = False
 318          self.snr_threshold = snr_threshold
 319  
 320      @staticmethod
 321      def parse_option(row, arg):
 322          safe_dict = {'max': max, 'min': min}
 323          safe_dict.update(row.__dict__)
 324          safe_dict.update(math.__dict__)
 325          safe_dict.update(pycbc.pnutils.__dict__)
 326          return eval(arg, {"__builtins__":None}, safe_dict)
 327  
 328      def cached_chisq_bins(self, template, psd):
 329          from pycbc.opt import LimitedSizeDict
 330  
 331          key = id(psd)
 332          if not hasattr(psd, '_chisq_cached_key'):
 333              psd._chisq_cached_key = {}
 334  
 335          if not hasattr(template, '_bin_cache'):
 336              template._bin_cache = LimitedSizeDict(size_limit=2**2)
 337  
 338          if key not in template._bin_cache or id(template.params) not in psd._chisq_cached_key:
 339              psd._chisq_cached_key[id(template.params)] = True
 340              num_bins = int(self.parse_option(template, self.num_bins))
 341  
 342              if hasattr(psd, 'sigmasq_vec') and \
 343                      template.approximant in psd.sigmasq_vec:
 344                  kmin = int(template.f_lower / psd.delta_f)
 345                  kmax = template.end_idx
 346                  bins = power_chisq_bins_from_sigmasq_series(
 347                      psd.sigmasq_vec[template.approximant],
 348                      num_bins,
 349                      kmin,
 350                      kmax
 351                  )
 352              else:
 353                  bins = power_chisq_bins(template, num_bins, psd, template.f_lower)
 354              template._bin_cache[key] = bins
 355  
 356          return template._bin_cache[key]
 357  
 358      def values(self, corr, snrv, snr_norm, psd, indices, template):
 359          """ Calculate the chisq at points given by indices.
 360  
 361          Returns
 362          -------
 363          chisq: Array
 364              Chisq values, one for each sample index, or zero for points below
 365              the specified SNR threshold
 366  
 367          chisq_dof: Array
 368              Number of statistical degrees of freedom for the chisq test
 369              in the given template, equal to 2 * num_bins - 2
 370          """
 371          if self.do:
 372              num_above = len(indices)
 373              dof = -100
 374              if self.snr_threshold:
 375                  above = abs(snrv * snr_norm) > self.snr_threshold
 376                  num_above = above.sum()
 377                  logging.info('%s above chisq activation threshold' % num_above)
 378                  above_indices = indices[above]
 379                  above_snrv = snrv[above]
 380                  chisq_out = numpy.zeros(len(indices), dtype=numpy.float32)
 381              else:
 382                  above_indices = indices
 383                  above_snrv = snrv
 384  
 385              if num_above > 0:
 386                  bins = self.cached_chisq_bins(template, psd)
 387                  # len(bins) is number of bin edges, num_bins = len(bins) - 1
 388                  dof = (len(bins) - 1) * 2 - 2
 389                  _chisq = power_chisq_at_points_from_precomputed(corr,
 390                                       above_snrv, snr_norm, bins, above_indices)
 391  
 392              if self.snr_threshold:
 393                  if num_above > 0:
 394                      chisq_out[above] = _chisq
 395              else:
 396                  if num_above == 0:
 397                      chisq_out = numpy.zeros(0, dtype=numpy.float32)
 398                  else:
 399                      chisq_out = _chisq
 400  
 401              return chisq_out, numpy.repeat(dof, len(indices))# dof * numpy.ones_like(indices)
 402          else:
 403              return None, None

 406  class SingleDetSkyMaxPowerChisq(SingleDetPowerChisq):
 407      """Class that handles precomputation and memory management for efficiently
 408      running the power chisq in a single detector inspiral analysis when
 409      maximizing analytically over sky location.
 410      """
 411      def __init__(self, **kwds):
 412          super(SingleDetSkyMaxPowerChisq, self).__init__(**kwds)
 413          self.template_mem = None
 414          self.corr_mem = None
 415  
 416      def calculate_chisq_bins(self, template, psd):
 417          """ Obtain the chisq bins for this template and PSD.
 418          """
 419          num_bins = int(self.parse_option(template, self.num_bins))
 420          if hasattr(psd, 'sigmasq_vec') and \
 421                                         template.approximant in psd.sigmasq_vec:
 422              kmin = int(template.f_lower / psd.delta_f)
 423              kmax = template.end_idx
 424              bins = power_chisq_bins_from_sigmasq_series(
 425                     psd.sigmasq_vec[template.approximant], num_bins, kmin, kmax)
 426          else:
 427              bins = power_chisq_bins(template, num_bins, psd, template.f_lower)
 428          return bins
 429  
 430      def values(self, corr_plus, corr_cross, snrv, psd,
 431                 indices, template_plus, template_cross, u_vals,
 432                 hplus_cross_corr, hpnorm, hcnorm):
 433          """ Calculate the chisq at points given by indices.
 434  
 435          Returns
 436          -------
 437          chisq: Array
 438              Chisq values, one for each sample index
 439  
 440          chisq_dof: Array
 441              Number of statistical degrees of freedom for the chisq test
 442              in the given template
 443          """
 444          if self.do:
 445              num_above = len(indices)
 446              if self.snr_threshold:
 447                  above = abs(snrv) > self.snr_threshold
 448                  num_above = above.sum()
 449                  logging.info('%s above chisq activation threshold' % num_above)
 450                  above_indices = indices[above]
 451                  above_snrv = snrv[above]
 452                  u_vals = u_vals[above]
 453                  rchisq = numpy.zeros(len(indices), dtype=numpy.float32)
 454                  dof = -100
 455              else:
 456                  above_indices = indices
 457                  above_snrv = snrv
 458  
 459              if num_above > 0:
 460                  chisq = []
 461                  curr_tmplt_mult_fac = 0.
 462                  curr_corr_mult_fac = 0.
 463                  if self.template_mem is None or \
 464                          (not len(self.template_mem) == len(template_plus)):
 465                      self.template_mem = zeros(len(template_plus),
 466                                  dtype=complex_same_precision_as(corr_plus))
 467                  if self.corr_mem is None or \
 468                                  (not len(self.corr_mem) == len(corr_plus)):
 469                      self.corr_mem = zeros(len(corr_plus),
 470                                  dtype=complex_same_precision_as(corr_plus))
 471  
 472                  tmplt_data = template_cross.data
 473                  corr_data = corr_cross.data
 474                  numpy.copyto(self.template_mem.data, template_cross.data)
 475                  numpy.copyto(self.corr_mem.data, corr_cross.data)
 476                  template_cross._data = self.template_mem.data
 477                  corr_cross._data = self.corr_mem.data
 478  
 479                  for lidx, index in enumerate(above_indices):
 480                      above_local_indices = numpy.array([index])
 481                      above_local_snr = numpy.array([above_snrv[lidx]])
 482                      local_u_val = u_vals[lidx]
 483                      # Construct template from _plus and _cross
 484                      # Note that this modifies in place, so we store that and
 485                      # revert on the next pass.
 486                      template = template_cross.multiply_and_add(template_plus,
 487                                                 local_u_val-curr_tmplt_mult_fac)
 488                      curr_tmplt_mult_fac = local_u_val
 489  
 490                      template.f_lower = template_plus.f_lower
 491                      template.params = template_plus.params
 492                      # Construct the corr vector
 493                      norm_fac = local_u_val*local_u_val + 1
 494                      norm_fac += 2 * local_u_val * hplus_cross_corr
 495                      norm_fac = hcnorm / (norm_fac**0.5)
 496                      hp_fac = local_u_val * hpnorm / hcnorm
 497                      corr = corr_cross.multiply_and_add(corr_plus,
 498                                                     hp_fac - curr_corr_mult_fac)
 499                      curr_corr_mult_fac = hp_fac
 500  
 501                      bins = self.calculate_chisq_bins(template, psd)
 502                      dof = (len(bins) - 1) * 2 - 2
 503                      curr_chisq = power_chisq_at_points_from_precomputed(corr,
 504                                            above_local_snr/ norm_fac, norm_fac,
 505                                            bins, above_local_indices)
 506                      chisq.append(curr_chisq[0])
 507                  chisq = numpy.array(chisq)
 508                  # Must reset corr and template to original values!
 509                  template_cross._data = tmplt_data
 510                  corr_cross._data = corr_data
 511  
 512              if self.snr_threshold:
 513                  if num_above > 0:
 514                      rchisq[above] = chisq
 515              else:
 516                  rchisq = chisq
 517  
 518              return rchisq, numpy.repeat(dof, len(indices))# dof * numpy.ones_like(indices)
 519          else:
 520              return None, None

  98                  for i in range(n):

 132  def chisq_accum_bin_numpy(chisq, q):
 133      chisq += q.squared_norm()

 135  def chisq_accum_bin(chisq, q):
 136      chisq = numpy.array(chisq.data, copy=False)
 137      q = numpy.array(q.data, copy=False)
 138      N = len(chisq)
 139      chisq_accum_bin_cython(chisq, q, N)

 141  def shift_sum(v1, shifts, bins):
 142      real_type = real_same_precision_as(v1)
 143      shifts = numpy.array(shifts, dtype=real_type)
 144  
 145      bins = numpy.array(bins, dtype=numpy.uint32)
 146      blen = len(bins) - 1 #
 147      v1 = numpy.array(v1.data, copy=False)
 148      slen = len(v1)
 149      n = int(len(shifts))
 150  
 151      # Create some output memory
 152      chisq = numpy.zeros(n, dtype=real_type)
 153  
 154      point_chisq_code(chisq, v1, n, slen, shifts, bins, blen)
 155  
 156      return  chisq

  34  def chisq_accum_bin(chisq, q):
  35      """Accumulate squared magnitude of q into chisq time series in JAX."""
  36      _ensure_x64()
  37      q_arr = to_jax(q)
  38      power = q_arr.real ** 2 + q_arr.imag ** 2
  39      if isinstance(chisq, JAXArrayData):
  40          chisq.set_array(chisq.array + power)
  41      elif hasattr(chisq, "_data") and isinstance(chisq._data, JAXArrayData):
  42          chisq._data.set_array(chisq._data.array + power)
  43      elif hasattr(chisq, "data") and isinstance(chisq.data, JAXArrayData):
  44          chisq.data.set_array(chisq.data.array + power)
  45      else:
  46          try:
  47              chisq.data[:] += np.asarray(power)
  48          except Exception:
  49              chisq[:] += np.asarray(power)

  57  def _array_is_cpu(arr):
  58      """Return whether an array is on CPU (including ordinary NumPy arrays)."""
  59      dev = getattr(arr, "device", None)
  60      if callable(dev):
  61          dev = dev()
  62      if dev is None:
  63          buffer = getattr(arr, "device_buffer", None)
  64          if buffer is not None:
  65              dev = getattr(buffer, "device", None)
  66              if callable(dev):
  67                  dev = dev()
  68      platform = getattr(dev, "platform", None)
  69      return platform in (None, "cpu")

  72  def _point_chisq_cpu(arr, shifts, bins, n_time, base_k=0):
  73      """Evaluate full or cropped CPU correlations with accurate Fourier sums."""
  74      return _point_chisq_numpy(arr, shifts, bins, n_time, base_k=base_k)

  76  
  77  def _require_point_chisq_x64():
  78      if not jax.config.jax_enable_x64:
  79          raise RuntimeError(
  80              "JAX point chi-square requires 64-bit integer phase arithmetic. "
  81              "Set PYCBC_JAX_ENABLE_X64=1 (the default) or use the CPU scheme."
  82          )
  83  
  84  
  85  def _time_shift_phase(n_slice, kmin, points, n_time, dtype):
  86      """Form periodic phases without losing bits in large frequency/time products."""
  87      _require_point_chisq_x64()
  88      k = jnp.arange(n_slice, dtype=jnp.int64) + jnp.asarray(kmin, jnp.int64)
  89      cycles = (k[:, None] * points[None, :].astype(jnp.int64)) % jnp.asarray(
  90          n_time, jnp.int64
  91      )
  92      angle = cycles.astype(jnp.float64) * (2 * jnp.pi / n_time)
  93      return jnp.exp(1j * angle).astype(dtype)

  96  @functools.partial(jax.jit, static_argnames=("chunk_size",))
  97  def _shift_sum_gpu_core(
  98      arr_slice, kmin_f, pts_chunk, bin_rel_indices, n_time_f, chunk_size=16
  99  ):
 100      """JIT-compiled GPU power chisq prefix sum across frequency bins on corr_slice."""
 101      n_slice = arr_slice.shape[0]
 102      phases = _time_shift_phase(
 103          n_slice, kmin_f, pts_chunk, n_time_f, arr_slice.dtype
 104      )
 105      weighted = arr_slice[:, None] * phases
 106      C = jnp.cumsum(weighted, axis=0)
 107      C_padded = jnp.pad(C, ((1, 0), (0, 0)))
 108      edges = jnp.clip(bin_rel_indices, 0, n_slice)
 109      i0 = edges[:-1]
 110      i1 = edges[1:]
 111      zb = C_padded[i1] - C_padded[i0]
 112      power = jnp.sum(zb.real ** 2 + zb.imag ** 2, axis=0)
 113      return power

 118      corr_tensor, row_idx, kmin_f, pts_chunk, bin_rel_indices, n_time_f, chunk_size=16
 119  ):
 120      """JIT-compiled GPU power chisq prefix sum indexing row on device."""
 121      arr_slice = corr_tensor[row_idx]
 122      n_slice = arr_slice.shape[0]
 123      phases = _time_shift_phase(
 124          n_slice, kmin_f, pts_chunk, n_time_f, arr_slice.dtype
 125      )
 126      weighted = arr_slice[:, None] * phases
 127      C = jnp.cumsum(weighted, axis=0)
 128      C_padded = jnp.pad(C, ((1, 0), (0, 0)))
 129      edges = jnp.clip(bin_rel_indices, 0, n_slice)
 130      i0 = edges[:-1]
 131      i1 = edges[1:]
 132      zb = C_padded[i1] - C_padded[i0]
 133      power = jnp.sum(zb.real ** 2 + zb.imag ** 2, axis=0)
 134      return power

 137  @functools.partial(jax.jit, static_argnames=("bucket_size",))
 138  def _batched_points_chisq_core(
 139      corr_tensor, row_indices, pts, bins_rel_all, kmin_f, n_time_f, bucket_size=256
 140  ):
 141      """JIT-compiled GPU batched power chisq prefix sum across all triggered points.
 142  
 143      Calculates time-shifted frequency bin sums for all points across all templates
 144      in parallel via vmap over points, executing in a single CUDA kernel.
 145      """
 146      n_slice = corr_tensor.shape[-1]
 147      def _point_chisq(row, pt, bin_rel):
 148          phases = _time_shift_phase(
 149              n_slice, kmin_f, jnp.reshape(pt, (1,)), n_time_f, row.dtype
 150          )[:, 0]
 151          weighted = row * phases
 152          C = jnp.cumsum(weighted)
 153          C_padded = jnp.pad(C, (1, 0))
 154          edges = jnp.clip(bin_rel, 0, n_slice)
 155          i0 = edges[:-1]
 156          i1 = edges[1:]
 157          zb = C_padded[i1] - C_padded[i0]
 158          return jnp.sum(zb.real ** 2 + zb.imag ** 2)
 159  
 160      rows = corr_tensor[row_indices]
 161      bins_pts = bins_rel_all[row_indices]
 162      return jax.vmap(_point_chisq)(rows, pts, bins_pts)

 165  def shift_sum(corr, points, bins):
 166      """Calculate time-shifted sum of FrequencySeries bins in JAX."""
 167      _ensure_x64()
 168      pts = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.int64)
 169      if len(pts) == 0:
 170          return np.array([], dtype=np.float32)
 171  
 172      use_row_indexing = (
 173          hasattr(corr, "_batch_tensor")
 174          and hasattr(corr, "_batch_pos")
 175          and corr._batch_tensor is not None
 176      )
 177  
 178      if use_row_indexing:
 179          arr = to_jax(corr._batch_tensor)
 180      else:
 181          arr = to_jax(corr)
 182      is_cpu = _array_is_cpu(arr)
 183  
 184      if is_cpu:
 185          if use_row_indexing:
 186              arr = arr[corr._batch_pos]
 187          arr_np = np.asarray(arr)
 188          base_k = int(getattr(corr, "_kmin", 0))
 189          n_time = int(getattr(corr, "_tlen", len(arr_np)))
 190          return _point_chisq_cpu(arr_np, pts, bins, n_time, base_k=base_k)
 191  
 192      _require_point_chisq_x64()
 193      if use_row_indexing:
 194          corr_tensor = to_jax(corr._batch_tensor)
 195          row_idx = int(corr._batch_pos)
 196          kmin = int(corr._kmin)
 197          n_time = int(corr._tlen)
 198      elif hasattr(corr, "_kmin") and hasattr(corr, "_tlen"):
 199          kmin = int(corr._kmin)
 200          n_time = int(corr._tlen)
 201          arr_slice = arr
 202      else:
 203          # Correlations contain the full complex FFT work vector, even
 204          # when represented by a FrequencySeries.
 205          n_time = len(arr)
 206          kmin = int(bins[0])
 207          kmax = int(bins[-1])
 208          arr_slice = arr[kmin:kmax]
 209  
 210      bin_indices = jnp.asarray(bins, dtype=jnp.int32)
 211      bin_rel = bin_indices - kmin
 212      kmin_f = float(kmin)
 213      n_time_f = float(n_time)
 214  
 215      pts_np = np.asarray(pts, dtype=np.int32)
 216      n_pts = len(pts_np)
 217      out_res = np.empty(n_pts, dtype=np.float32)
 218  
 219      offset = 0
 220      while offset < n_pts:
 221          rem = n_pts - offset
 222          if rem == 1:
 223              sz = 1
 224          elif rem == 2:
 225              sz = 2
 226          elif rem <= 4:
 227              sz = 4
 228          elif rem <= 8:
 229              sz = 8
 230          else:
 231              sz = 16
 232          chunk_slice = pts_np[offset:offset + min(rem, sz)]
 233          cur_len = len(chunk_slice)
 234          if cur_len < sz:
 235              buf = np.zeros(sz, dtype=np.int32)
 236              buf[:cur_len] = chunk_slice
 237              pts_j = jax.device_put(buf)
 238          else:
 239              pts_j = jax.device_put(chunk_slice)
 240          if use_row_indexing:
 241              res_j = _shift_sum_gpu_core_row(
 242                  corr_tensor, row_idx, kmin_f, pts_j, bin_rel, n_time_f, chunk_size=sz
 243              )
 244          else:
 245              res_j = _shift_sum_gpu_core(
 246                  arr_slice, kmin_f, pts_j, bin_rel, n_time_f, chunk_size=sz
 247              )
 248          out_res[offset:offset + cur_len] = np.asarray(res_j)[:cur_len]
 249          offset += cur_len
 250      return out_res

 253  def power_chisq_at_points_from_precomputed(
 254      corr, snr, snr_norm, bins, indices
 255  ):
 256      """Calculate chisq values at triggered points from precomputed products."""
 257      num_bins = len(bins) - 1
 258      chisq = shift_sum(corr, indices, bins)
 259      snr_arr = np.asarray(snr)
 260      return (
 261          (chisq * num_bins - (snr_arr.conj() * snr_arr).real)
 262          * (float(snr_norm) ** 2.0)
 263      )

 266  def power_chisq_bins_jax(
 267      htilde,
 268      num_bins,
 269      psd,
 270      low_frequency_cutoff=None,
 271      high_frequency_cutoff=None,
 272  ):
 273      """Calculate standard-backend-compatible bin edges for a JAX template."""
 274      from pycbc.filter.matchedfilter import get_cutoff_indices
 275  
 276      _ensure_x64()
 277      n_pts = (len(htilde) - 1) * 2
 278      delta_f = float(htilde.delta_f)
 279      kmin, kmax = get_cutoff_indices(
 280          low_frequency_cutoff, high_frequency_cutoff, delta_f, n_pts
 281      )
 282  
 283      from pycbc import scheme
 284      state = getattr(scheme.mgr, "state", None)
 285      target_dev = getattr(state, "jax_device", None)
 286  
 287      h_arr = to_jax(htilde, device=target_dev)
 288      psd_arr = to_jax(psd, device=target_dev)
 289  
 290      return _power_chisq_bins_numpy(
 291          h_arr, psd_arr, int(kmin), int(kmax), int(num_bins), delta_f
 292      )
 293  
 294  
 295  def _power_chisq_bins_numpy(h_arr, psd_arr, kmin, kmax, num_bins, delta_f):
 296      """Match the standard backend's cumulative power and discrete bin edges.
 297  
 298      A parallel single-precision scan changes bin boundaries in long templates.
 299      Compute these cached boundaries with the same serial accumulation and
 300      edge precision as sigmasq_series/power_chisq_bins_from_sigmasq_series.
 301      """
 302      h_slice = np.asarray(h_arr)[..., kmin:kmax]
 303      power = h_slice.real ** 2 + h_slice.imag ** 2
 304      power /= np.asarray(psd_arr)[kmin:kmax]
 305      cumulative = np.cumsum(power, axis=-1) * (4.0 * delta_f)
 306  
 307      def row_bins(row):
 308          edges = np.arange(num_bins) * row[-1] / num_bins
 309          bins = np.searchsorted(row, edges, side="right") + kmin
 310          return np.append(bins, kmax).astype(np.uint32)
 311  
 312      if cumulative.ndim == 1:
 313          return row_bins(cumulative)
 314      return np.stack([row_bins(row) for row in cumulative])
 315

 317  def batch_power_chisq_bins_jax(
 318      templates,
 319      num_bins,
 320      psd,
 321      low_frequency_cutoff=None,
 322      high_frequency_cutoff=None,
 323  ):
 324      """Calculate standard-backend-compatible bin edges for JAX template rows."""
 325      from pycbc.filter.matchedfilter import get_cutoff_indices
 326  
 327      _ensure_x64()
 328      n_pts = (len(templates[0]) - 1) * 2
 329      delta_f = float(templates[0].delta_f)
 330      kmin, kmax = get_cutoff_indices(
 331          low_frequency_cutoff, high_frequency_cutoff, delta_f, n_pts
 332      )
 333  
 334      from pycbc import scheme
 335      state = getattr(scheme.mgr, "state", None)
 336      target_dev = getattr(state, "jax_device", None)
 337  
 338      batch_tensor = getattr(templates, "_batch_tensor", None)
 339      if batch_tensor is None:
 340          tmpls_tensor = jnp.stack([to_jax(t, device=target_dev) for t in templates], axis=0)
 341      else:
 342          tmpls_tensor = to_jax(batch_tensor, device=target_dev)
 343  
 344      psd_arr = to_jax(psd, device=target_dev)
 345  
 346      return _power_chisq_bins_numpy(
 347          tmpls_tensor,
 348          psd_arr,
 349          int(kmin),
 350          int(kmax),
 351          int(num_bins),
 352          delta_f,
 353      )

 356  def batch_power_chisq_jax(
 357      corr_tensor,
 358      batch_results,
 359      active_templates,
 360      psd,
 361      analyze_start,
 362      snr_threshold=None,
 363      power_chisq=None,
 364  ):
 365      """Batched evaluation of power chisq across all triggered templates in a segment.
 366  
 367      Computes time-shifted frequency bin sums for all triggered points across all
 368      templates simultaneously in a single JAX GPU kernel launch, replacing sequential
 369      per-template dispatch and synchronization loops.
 370  
 371      Returns:
 372          chisq_map: dict mapping act_pos -> (chisq_out, chisq_dof)
 373      """
 374      _ensure_x64()
 375      if corr_tensor is None or len(batch_results) == 0:
 376          return None
 377  
 378      psd_id = id(psd)
 379      b = len(active_templates)
 380  
 381      # 1. Gather bin edges for all active templates
 382      bins_list = []
 383      for tmpl in active_templates:
 384          b_edges = None
 385          # The canonical cache also validates template parameters; reusable
 386          # template buffers may retain edges belonging to a previous template.
 387          if power_chisq is not None and hasattr(power_chisq, "cached_chisq_bins"):
 388              b_edges = power_chisq.cached_chisq_bins(tmpl, psd)
 389          elif hasattr(tmpl, "_bin_cache") and psd_id in tmpl._bin_cache:
 390              b_edges = tmpl._bin_cache[psd_id]
 391          if b_edges is None:
 392              return None
 393          bins_list.append(b_edges)
 394  
 395      # Different bin counts require the caller's per-template scalar fallback.
 396      num_bins_set = set(len(b_edges) - 1 for b_edges in bins_list)
 397      if len(num_bins_set) != 1:
 398          return None
 399  
 400      num_bins = len(bins_list[0]) - 1
 401      dof = num_bins * 2 - 2
 402  
 403      # Retrieve correlation metadata
 404      corr_sample = None
 405      for res in batch_results:
 406          if res[2] is not None and hasattr(res[2], "_kmin"):
 407              corr_sample = res[2]
 408              break
 409      if corr_sample is None:
 410          return None
 411  
 412      kmin = int(corr_sample._kmin)
 413      tlen = int(corr_sample._tlen)
 414      kmin_f = float(kmin)
 415      n_time_f = float(tlen)
 416  
 417      # 2. Gather active trigger points across all templates
 418      chisq_map = {}
 419      points_to_compute = []
 420      total_points = 0
 421  
 422      for act_pos in range(b):
 423          snr, norm, corr, idx, snrv = batch_results[act_pos]
 424          n_idx = len(idx)
 425          if n_idx == 0:
 426              chisq_map[act_pos] = (
 427                  np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32), np.repeat(dof, 0)
 428              )
 429              continue
 430  
 431          if snr_threshold is not None:
 432              above = abs(snrv * norm) > snr_threshold
 433              n_above = int(np.sum(above))
 434          else:
 435              above = np.ones(n_idx, dtype=bool)
 436              n_above = n_idx
 437  
 438          if n_above == 0:
 439              chisq_map[act_pos] = (
 440                  np.zeros(n_idx, dtype=np.float32),
 441                  np.repeat(dof, n_idx),
 442              )
 443              continue
 444  
 445          above_indices = (idx[above] + analyze_start).astype(np.int32)
 446          above_snrv = snrv[above]
 447          points_to_compute.append({
 448              "act_pos": act_pos,
 449              "above_indices": above_indices,
 450              "above_snrv": above_snrv,
 451              "norm": float(norm),
 452              "above_mask": above,
 453              "n_idx": n_idx,
 454              "n_above": n_above,
 455          })
 456          total_points += n_above
 457  
 458      if total_points == 0:
 459          return chisq_map
 460  
 461      # 3. Stack bins array for active templates and build flattened point arrays
 462      bins_arr = np.array(bins_list, dtype=np.int32)
 463  
 464      all_rows = np.empty(total_points, dtype=np.int32)
 465      all_pts = np.empty(total_points, dtype=np.int32)
 466  
 467      offset = 0
 468      for item in points_to_compute:
 469          n_ab = item["n_above"]
 470          all_rows[offset:offset + n_ab] = item["act_pos"]
 471          all_pts[offset:offset + n_ab] = item["above_indices"]
 472          offset += n_ab
 473  
 474      # CPU correlations use the shared accurate Fourier sums. Grouping points
 475      # by template avoids a padded JAX bucket and keeps cropped rows intact.
 476      if _array_is_cpu(corr_tensor):
 477          corr_np = np.asarray(corr_tensor)
 478          all_shift_sums = np.empty(total_points, dtype=np.float32)
 479          offset = 0
 480          for item in points_to_compute:
 481              act_pos = item["act_pos"]
 482              n_ab = item["n_above"]
 483              if corr_np.ndim == 2:
 484                  row = corr_np[act_pos]
 485              else:
 486                  row = np.asarray(batch_results[act_pos][2].data)
 487              vals = _point_chisq_cpu(
 488                  row, item["above_indices"], bins_arr[act_pos], tlen, base_k=kmin
 489              )
 490              all_shift_sums[offset:offset + n_ab] = vals
 491              offset += n_ab
 492      else:
 493          _require_point_chisq_x64()
 494          bins_rel_all = jax.device_put(bins_arr - kmin)
 495          # 4. Bucketed JAX execution
 496          bucket_sizes = (32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096)
 497          chosen_bucket = None
 498          for bsz in bucket_sizes:
 499              if total_points <= bsz:
 500                  chosen_bucket = bsz
 501                  break
 502          if chosen_bucket is None:
 503              chosen_bucket = int(2 ** np.ceil(np.log2(total_points)))
 504  
 505          r_buf = np.zeros(chosen_bucket, dtype=np.int32)
 506          p_buf = np.zeros(chosen_bucket, dtype=np.int32)
 507          r_buf[:total_points] = all_rows
 508          p_buf[:total_points] = all_pts
 509  
 510          r_dev = jax.device_put(r_buf)
 511          p_dev = jax.device_put(p_buf)
 512  
 513          res_dev = _batched_points_chisq_core(
 514              corr_tensor, r_dev, p_dev, bins_rel_all, kmin_f, n_time_f, bucket_size=chosen_bucket
 515          )
 516          all_shift_sums = np.asarray(res_dev[:total_points])
 517  
 518      # 5. Distribute results back to each template
 519      offset = 0
 520      for item in points_to_compute:
 521          n_ab = item["n_above"]
 522          act_pos = item["act_pos"]
 523          n_idx = item["n_idx"]
 524          norm = item["norm"]
 525          above_mask = item["above_mask"]
 526          above_snrv = item["above_snrv"]
 527  
 528          shifts = all_shift_sums[offset:offset + n_ab]
 529          offset += n_ab
 530  
 531          chisq_vals = (shifts * num_bins - (above_snrv.conj() * above_snrv).real) * (norm ** 2.0)
 532          chisq_out = np.zeros(n_idx, dtype=np.float32)
 533          chisq_out[above_mask] = chisq_vals.astype(np.float32)
 534          chisq_dof = np.repeat(dof, n_idx)
 535  
 536          chisq_map[act_pos] = (chisq_out, chisq_dof)
 537  
 538      return chisq_map

   1  """NumPy point chi-square used by the JAX backend on CPU devices.
   2  
   3  Native CPUScheme dispatch retains its existing compiled implementation.
   4  """
   5  
   6  import numpy as np
   7  
   8  
   9  def shift_sum(corr, points, bins, n_time=None, base_k=0):
  10      """Sum squared bin amplitudes using double-precision Fourier phases.
  11  
  12      ``bins`` contains absolute frequency indices. ``base_k`` identifies the
  13      first frequency of a cropped correlation, whose full FFT length must be
  14      supplied as ``n_time``. Return the correlation's real precision, but form
  15      phases, complex sums, and accumulated power in double precision.
  16  
  17      Frequencies are processed in bounded chunks for each selected sample;
  18      storage does not grow with the number of samples or the FFT length.
  19      """
  20      corr = np.asarray(corr)
  21      points = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.int64)
  22      bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=np.int64)
  23      n_time = len(corr) if n_time is None else int(n_time)
  24      output = np.empty(len(points), dtype=corr.real.dtype)
  25      chunk_size = 65536
  26      for index, point in enumerate(points):
  27          total_power = 0.0
  28          point = point % n_time
  29          for start, end in zip(bins[:-1], bins[1:]):
  30              amplitude = 0j
  31              # Cropped correlations represent zero power outside their stored
  32              # frequency interval; retain the original bins, including empties.
  33              start = max(start, base_k)
  34              end = min(end, base_k + len(corr))
  35              for offset in range(start, end, chunk_size):
  36                  stop = min(offset + chunk_size, end)
  37                  frequencies = np.arange(offset, stop, dtype=np.int64)
  38                  cycles = (frequencies * point) % n_time
  39                  phase = np.exp((2j * np.pi / n_time) * cycles)
  40                  amplitude += np.sum(
  41                      corr[offset-base_k:stop-base_k] * phase,
  42                      dtype=np.complex128,
  43                  )
  44              total_power += amplitude.real ** 2 + amplitude.imag ** 2
  45          output[index] = total_power
  46      return output
